s1.syndrome_frame: chronic, painful, growing tumor on the buttock with secondary infection and possible viral etiology
salient_findings: growing, painful tumor on the right buttock
verrucous, exophytic tumor with scant yellow drainage
positive for HSV type 2 and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus
key_facts: 8-month history of a growing tumor
tumor located on the right medial buttock
tumor extends to the perianal skin
patient has chronic kidney disease
patient has genital herpes simplex virus (HSV)
no history of genital warts, HIV, or inflammatory bowel disease
physical examination findings revealed a 5 × 7-cm tumor
bacterial cultures grew methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus
microbial cultures were negative for deep fungal infection and acid-fast bacteria
biopsy and histology showed hyperplastic epidermis with ulceration, necrosis, and dense inflammatory infiltrate
immunohistochemistry showed positive staining for herpes simplex virus types 1 and 2

shortlist.label: Verrucous carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: matches the clinical description of a growing, painful tumor with verrucous appearance

shortlist.label: Giant condyloma acuminatum
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with the patient's history of genital herpes simplex virus and the tumor's location and appearance

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: a possible diagnosis given the tumor's location, growth pattern, and histological findings

shortlist.label: Herpes simplex virus infection
shortlist.why_kept: supported by the patient's history of genital HSV and the positive immunohistochemistry results

shortlist.label: Keratoacanthoma
shortlist.why_kept: a less likely but still plausible diagnosis given the tumor's rapid growth and histological features

raw.rationale: The patient's history of genital herpes simplex virus and the presence of a large, verrucous tumor on the perianal skin, along with the biopsy and histology findings, are consistent with giant condyloma acuminatum, which is a rare, sexually transmitted disease caused by human papillomavirus (HPV) that can present with similar clinical and histological features.

rejected.label: Verrucous carcinoma
rejected.why: While verrucous carcinoma can present with similar clinical features, the presence of HSV and the specific histological findings in this case make giant condyloma acuminatum a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Squamous cell carcinoma typically presents with more aggressive features and is less likely to be associated with HSV.

rejected.label: Herpes simplex virus infection
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of genital HSV and the tumor is positive for HSV, the clinical presentation and histological findings suggest a more complex diagnosis than a simple HSV infection.

rejected.label: Keratoacanthoma
rejected.why: Keratoacanthoma is a distinct clinical entity that typically presents as a solitary, rapidly growing nodule with a central crater, which is not consistent with the patient's presentation.
